name: Gemini 4 Neon
archDisplay: Proprietary model adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon; architecture and parameter count undisclosed; 1M-token context
note: Google DeepMind's mid-tier Gemini 4 model, released Nov 18, 2026 and rolling out to the Gemini API (AI Studio, paid tier only), Gemini for business, Google Antigravity and the Gemini app (Pro and Ultra). Google positions it between Carbon (hardest long-horizon work) and Hydrogen (fast everyday execution); the model card says it is 'adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon'. It is a sibling, not a successor, so predecessor is null (as with Hydrogen). Priced flat at $3/$15 per Mtok across the 1M-token window, cached input $0.15 (AI Studio docs, blog); no introductory wording. Four thinking levels (low, medium, high default, xhigh). Vals AI's independent runs (model page, xhigh, no fallbacks shown) add Terminal-Bench 4.0 61.62 (#7 of 69) and Terminal-Bench-Science 62.86 (#2 of 48); Vals Index 70.87 (#2 of 42) has no column. Self-reported rows come from the model card table (results as of November 2026; comparison columns Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol). NOT FILED: Terminal-Bench 4.1 cheating-adjusted 65.2, Agents' Last Exam v1.1 75.8, CursorBench 4.1 65.4 and FrontierCode 2.0 46.2 (newer versions than the corpus columns); CWE-Bench v2 70.7 (above the column's bounds, as with Carbon's 71.0); HLE-Diamond 71.3 (subset); SWE-sweep (39.0 provider harness, 12.8 mini-SWE), RiemannBench 84.0, MKA 56.5, GraphWalks 95.2, WebExploitBench v1.2 51.3, AA Index 61 and Vals Index v2.2 70.9 (no corpus column); and, from the blog, Vending-Bench 2 $16,843, Agent Arena Index 1336, AA Coding Agent Index 58.6 and AutoBaxBench hard tier 76% (no corpus column). The card's Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol comparison figures are not filed as rows for those models. No ARC Prize or Text Arena result yet.
